Building in a row restricts the possibilities for direct lighting to two façades so that, with economic building depths of up to 12 m and widths between 4 and 8 m, the existence of a badly lit or dark middle zone containing the stairs, subsidiary rooms and often also the dining area becomes unavoidable.
Entrance recesses should be at least 1.25 m (better 1.50 m) wide and approx. 1.00 m deep, so that two people can wait comfortably and protected in front of the door
According to the building regulations, every house or flat must have at least one kitchen or kitchenette for cooking.
The building regulations require that every flat or house be provided with a sufficiently large storeroom.
Setback areas are the spaces between buildings and their plot boundaries.
According to the model building regulations (MBO), it is 0.4 × H, but at least 3 m (0.2 × H, min. 3 m for commercial and industrial areas).
In front of the outside walls of building classes 1 and 2 with not more than three overground storeys, 3 m depth is also sufficient.
Wall height means the dimension from ground level to upper extent of the wall or to the intersection of the wall with the roof covering
Setback areas must be on the plot itself
The height of roofs with a pitch of ≤70° is included to one third, ≥70° fully with the wall height

The net floor area is the sum of the usable area (area which serves the building’s intended purpose), the technical function area (rooms for building services, such as utility connection room, accessible shafts, etc.) and the traffic area (e.g. stairwells, corridors, lift shafts, escape balconies etc.).

The following do not belong to the letting area: stairs, lifts, emergency exits, escape balconies, services rooms, shafts, protection rooms, areas of columns, pillars and separate walls, areas with a clear ceiling height of 1.50 m or less.
2. Areas with communal right of use, individually listed as: rooms for communal use (WCs/bathrooms, staff rooms, etc.) and communal traffic areas (entrance halls, corridors, etc.).

Escape routes are min. 1.25 m wide and should if possible lead in two directions, to each staircase. The maximum walking distance from each point of an occupied room may not exceed 25 m. Corridors with two escape directions may be max. 40 m long. After 20 m, a smoke-proof self-closing door must be installed. Branch corridors with only one escape direction may be max. 10 m long. If a second escape route (e.g. an escape balcony) is available, max. 20 m.
In order to avoid fire spreading from one storey to the one above, there must be W 90 A fire-resistant parapets at least 1 m high (fire spreading height).
Alternatively, a W 90 A horizontal building element projecting at least 1.5 m from the façade can be provided.

All-glass façades (also double façades) are permitted only with special approvals if particular protection measures (area sprinklers, mist extinguishing systems) can prevent the spread of fire to the next storey
Closures between stairways and corridors legally essential as escape routes and also for the division of legally essential corridors more than 30 m long must be self-closing and smoke-proof
For more than 10 employees, a rest/break room is necessary (workplace regulations).
Seminar rooms, usual sizes: 20, 40, 50, 60 seats; mobile double tables, width 1.20 m, depth 0.60 m, space required per student 1.90–2.00 m.
If there is free ventilation from only one external wall, the depth of the room should not exceed 2.5 × clear ceiling height.
